Repeater line N = 6 gt (track delay, family delay-rep6: N = 6 + 8n gt, n = 0): a delay-3 repeater then 0 delay-4 repeater(s) in a row on stones, each reading the one before; N = 2 gt per redstone tick of delay

Repeater line N = 8 gt (track delay, family delay-rep8: N = 8 + 8n gt, n = 0): a delay-4 repeater then 0 delay-4 repeater(s) in a row on stones, each reading the one before; N = 2 gt per redstone tick of delay

Torch tower N = 6 gt (track delay, family delay-torch: N = 6 + 4n gt, n = 0): a repeater powers a block, 2 torches climb from it (each torch powers the block above it, the next torch stands on that block): N = 2 + 2 x 2 gt, non-inverting with an even count

Repeater line N = 2 gt (track delay, family delay-rep2: N = 2 + 8n gt, n = 0): a delay-1 repeater then 0 delay-4 repeater(s) in a row on stones, each reading the one before; N = 2 gt per redstone tick of delay
Comparator line N = 2 gt (track delay, family delay-cmp: N = 2 + 2n gt, n = 0): 1 compare-mode comparator(s) in a row on stones, 2 gt each; keeps pulses down to 2-3 gt

Instant delay line (N = 0 gt) with real signal inputs: the input dust powers the dust beside it, and the sticky piston quasi-connected to the input cell pushes its block next to the output cell, holding it on for the gt after the fall. Under R7 the input changes during a tick, so the piston acts in that same tick: this design measured N = 1 when the judge placed a redstone block in the input cell, and measures N = 0 now. after the fall, until the piston pulls it back 1 gt after the fall.
